question: What is the primary focus of health promotion in midwifery practice?

options.A: Treating advanced infectious diseases with antibiotics
options.B: Writing policy guidelines for national health ministries
options.C: Performing emergency surgical procedures in the ward
options.D: Enabling people to increase control over their health

explanation: Health promotion is fundamentally about empowering individuals and communities to take charge of their own well-being and health determinants. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why does preventing complications like eclampsia often start long before labor begins?

options.A: Because pregnant women rarely visit the hospital until delivery day
options.B: Because labor wards lack the equipment to manage high blood pressure
options.C: Because early health education and antenatal talks help detect risks early
options.D: Because surgical interventions can only be planned months in advance

explanation: Antenatal health education allows midwives to spot warning signs and educate women on danger signs before acute emergencies develop. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h1)

question: When do pregnant and postnatal women learn most effectively during health education sessions?

options.A: When the information is directly relevant to their daily lived experiences
options.B: When the midwife uses advanced medical terminology and Latin names
options.C: When the session focuses entirely on rare textbook disease conditions
options.D: When the mother sits quietly without asking any questions at all

explanation: Learners retain information much better when it connects directly to their current real-world needs and life stages. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h2)

question: A midwife is teaching breastfeeding attachment to a new mother in the postnatal ward. Which action demonstrates active participation?

options.A: Asking the mother to demonstrate the latch herself and checking her technique
options.B: Lecturing the group for an hour about the hormonal anatomy of lactation
options.C: Handing the mother a printed pamphlet and telling her to read it quietly
options.D: Demonstrating the technique on a plastic doll while the mothers watch

explanation: Active participation involves the learner physically engaging with the skill rather than just listening or watching passively. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which setting is most appropriate for discussing sensitive issues like a positive HIV status?

options.A: A public community town hall meeting outside
options.B: A loud group health talk in the main waiting hall
options.C: An open discussion during routine ward rounds

explanation: Sensitive personal health matters require privacy and confidentiality to protect the patient and build clinical trust. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of using group health talks during antenatal clinic days?

options.A: They replace the need for individual physical examinations entirely
options.B: They eliminate all language and cultural barriers in the room
options.C: They efficiently deliver general wellness topics to many mothers at once
options.D: They guarantee that every patient will disclose private trauma

explanation: Group health talks save time and educate multiple women simultaneously on broad preventive health topics. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common communication barrier in diverse clinical maternity settings?

options.A: Language differences between the midwife and client
options.B: Intimidating power dynamics in the hospital setup
options.D: Conflicting traditional cultural beliefs about birth

explanation: Electronic record systems affect administration or documentation, but language gaps, cultural clashes, and intimidating power dynamics are the direct interpersonal communication barriers. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h4)

question: A pregnant teenager in the antenatal clinic looks down and refuses to speak when asked about her diet. What communication barrier is most likely operating here?

options.A: Advanced neurological disease affecting speech production centers
options.B: An absolute physical hearing impairment requiring surgical referral
options.C: Intimidating power dynamics between the young client and health worker
options.D: Complete language translation failure due to a foreign dialect

explanation: Young or vulnerable patients often feel intimidated by healthcare authority figures, leading to withdrawal and reluctance to speak. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h4)

question: Who should midwives collaborate with when planning community-level health education sessions?

options.A: Private security contractors stationed at the hospital gates
options.B: Only international medical researchers and pharmaceutical company reps
options.C: Federal legislators and national tax collection board officers
options.D: Local opinion leaders, traditional birth attendants, and community elders

explanation: Grassroots success relies heavily on partnering with respected figures within that specific community. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important to use visual aids featuring local imagery and food items during health talks?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for the midwife to speak at all
options.B: It helps the audience connect personally with the health message
options.C: It lowers the financial printing cost of textbooks for the hospital
options.D: It is a strict legal requirement set by international donor agencies

explanation: Relatable visual cues make abstract health advice feel real, achievable, and culturally appropriate for the listeners. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating midwife-led health education sessions?

options.A: To test the spelling and grammar skills of the nursing students
options.B: To assess whether health education actually changes behaviors and outcomes
options.C: To fulfill administrative paperwork requirements for hospital accreditation
options.D: To penalize patients who fail to memorize the antenatal lecture notes

explanation: Evaluation measures whether the teaching successfully translated into better health practices and reduced complications. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h6)

question: Pregnant women in a clinic keep using harmful herbal concoctions despite previous lectures. What should the midwife do next?

options.A: Report all attendees to the local police station for criminal negligence
options.B: Stop conducting health education entirely since patients never listen
options.C: Increase the speed of the lectures so meetings finish much faster
options.D: Revise the communication strategy and delivery method to address root beliefs

explanation: Persistent unsafe practices indicate that the current educational approach is ineffective and needs adaptation, not abandonment. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h6)
